lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The café near the station, the one open at weird hours for people with weird hours. Someone at the counter is reading the book you own two copies of.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.text: They always burn the espresso here. We keep coming anyway.

beats.prompt: They nod at the book in your hand — same cover.

choices.label: Two copies, actually. One to lend, one to keep.
I only read it on nights I can't sleep. So — often.
Don't tell me how it ends. I've stopped three times.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.text: A lender AND a keeper. Rare.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They set the book down like they've decided the conversation is worth more than the chapter.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.text: Weird hours, huh. Let me guess — you're either a nurse or you're running from something.

beats.prompt: How much do you give away?

choices.label: 911 dispatch. I run TOWARD the something.
Little of both. It's a long story and cold coffee.
Let's just say I'm good in a crisis.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.text: Then I'm safe. Good to know.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The barista calls the next order and doesn't call yours. The moment stretches, warm, waiting on you.

choices.label: 'Great book. Terrible espresso.' Stay and talk.
Nod politely and take your cup to go.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.text: Okay, burnt espresso tastes better free.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You trade a smile and a phone number scribbled on a napkin. The walk home feels shorter than the map says it is.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Twenty minutes become forty — the book, the city, the espresso. No numbers exchanged, but this café keeps weird hours, and so do you both. You'll be back tomorrow. So will they.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You take the cup and the exit. Through the window, the reader turns a page. Maybe next time — you tell yourself, and almost believe it.
